harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented traffic mirroring so node3 receives a copy of all traffic exchanged between node1 and node2 on their shared L2 segment, while node1<->node2 traffic itself is unaffected. Shared segment: node1 eth1 / node2 enp8s0 / node3 enp8s0 (192.168.50.0/24, freshly addressed — none had IPv4 before). Confirmed baseline: this segment is switch-like (learning), so node3 saw zero node1<->node2 packets before any change. Implementation: a GRETAP tunnel (node1 192.168.50.1 <-> node3 192.168.50.3) plus Linux tc (clsact qdisc, flower filters matching node2's IP in both directions, mirred egress-mirror action) on node1's eth1, mirroring ingress and egress node1<->node2 traffic into the tunnel non-disruptively (mirred 'mirror', not 'redirect'). Verified node3's gretap1 interface shows the exact original (unencapsulated after decap) ICMP request/reply packets addressed to 192.168.50.1/192.168.50.2, while concurrent pings between node1 and node2 show 0% packet loss throughout. Found and fixed a real obstacle along the way: NetworkManager on node2/node3 silently dropped the manually assigned IPs (unmanaged-interface reconciliation), fixed with persistent nmcli connection profiles; and node3's firewalld default 'public' zone rejected the GRE tunnel packets with 'admin-prohibited', fixed by binding enp8s0 to a dedicated 'mirror-segment' firewalld zone with protocol=gre allowed. Persisted all configuration: a systemd oneshot service on node1 (SONiC/Debian) recreates eth1 addressing, docker0/interfaces-config.service cleanup, the gretap1 tunnel, and tc mirror filters at boot (hardened with a carrier-wait retry loop after observing eth1 came up admin-UP but link-DOWN immediately post-reboot); NetworkManager profiles + firewalld zone persist node2/node3 config natively. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes (node2, then node3, then node1 last): captured pre-restart boot_id via /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, issued systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection), polled until exec was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed on every node, and re-verified full functional recovery (addressing, gretap tunnel, tc filters/counters, and a live end-to-end ping+tcpdump mirror test) after each restart — including a full working mirror test after node1's own restart, the last and most disruptive one.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology/interfaces/routes on node1, node2, node3
Identified shared segment: node1 eth1, node2 enp8s0, node3 enp8s0 (no IPv4 assigned initially)
Ran SONiC pre-config cleanup on node1 (docker0 down, stopped interfaces-config.service)
Assigned 192.168.50.0/24 addresses to eth1/enp8s0/enp8s0
Established and confirmed baseline node1<->node2 connectivity
Confirmed segment behaves like a learning switch: node3 saw 0 packets of node1<->node2 traffic pre-mirroring
Created GRETAP tunnels node1<->node3 (gretap1)
Configured tc clsact qdisc + flower filters with mirred egress-mirror action on node1 eth1 for node2's traffic (both directions)
Verified mirrored ICMP traffic appears on node3's gretap1 while node1<->node2 ping shows 0% loss
Diagnosed and fixed NetworkManager wiping manual IPs on node2/node3 via persistent nmcli connection profiles
Diagnosed and fixed node3 firewalld rejecting GRE tunnel traffic via a dedicated mirror-segment zone with protocol=gre allowed
Re-verified mirroring end-to-end after firewall fix
Created and installed systemd oneshot services on node1 (mirror setup script) and relied on NM profiles/firewalld zone on node2/node3 for boot persistence
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node2, node3, and node1 (in that order) one at a time via systemctl reboot, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled each node until exec was reachable again and confirmed changed boot_id for each
Hardened node1's boot script with a carrier-wait retry loop after observing eth1 came up admin-UP but link-DOWN post-reboot, then manually corrected and reinstalled the fixed script
Re-verified full mirroring recovery (addressing, gretap1, tc filters/counters, live ping+tcpdump test) after each of the three restarts, including after node1's own restart

evidence.requirement: node1<->node2 traffic keeps flowing normally after mirroring is configured
evidence.summary: Repeated pings from node1 eth1 to node2 (192.168.50.2) show 0% packet loss both before and after mirroring was applied (an earlier interim run showed spurious loss caused by node3's firewall rejecting GRE, resolved before this final set).

evidence.requirement: node3 receives a copy of node1<->node2 traffic despite being addressed elsewhere, and did NOT before mirroring was configured
evidence.summary: Baseline tcpdump on node3's enp8s0 captured 0 packets during a node1<->node2 ping (segment is switch-like/isolated). After configuring gretap1 + tc mirred mirroring on node1's eth1, tcpdump on node3's gretap1 captured all ICMP echo request/reply pairs addressed to 192.168.50.1/192.168.50.2 in both directions.

evidence.requirement: tc mirror filters are actively matching and mirroring traffic (not just configured)
evidence.summary: tc -s filter show on node1's eth1 ingress/egress clsact filters shows non-zero matched packet/byte counters for the mirred egress-mirror action, both before and after the node1 restart.

evidence.requirement: Root-cause and fix of NetworkManager silently dropping manual IP config on node2/node3
evidence.summary: Diagnosed enp8s0 IP disappearing due to NetworkManager marking it disconnected/unmanaged, then fixed by creating persistent nmcli 'mirror-lan' connection profiles on node2 and node3, confirmed IP restored and sticking.

evidence.requirement: Root-cause and fix of node3 firewalld blocking the GRE mirror tunnel
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's eth1 revealed node3 sending 'ICMP host unreachable - admin prohibited filter' in response to GRE mirror packets; traced to firewalld's default public zone; fixed by creating a dedicated 'mirror-segment' zone with protocol=gre allowed and binding enp8s0's NM connection to it persistently.

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - node1 (SONiC switch): healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id 8e8823ec..., issued backgrounded systemctl reboot (ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id c85393b1..., fixed a transient eth1 link-down state, then proved full mirroring recovery via a live ping+tcpdump mirror test and non-zero tc filter counters.

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - node2: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id 8f258838..., issued backgrounded reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id d7d93713..., and verified enp8s0's 192.168.50.2/24 address was restored automatically via the persisted NetworkManager profile.

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - node3: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id 21de1f79..., issued backgrounded reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id 7c113fa6..., and verified enp8s0's IP, the gretap1 tunnel, and the mirror-segment firewalld zone binding all recovered automatically.
